html:
The Waccamaw and the Woccon were Siouan-speaking peoples of the coastal plain of the Carolinas. The Waccamaw lived along the Waccamaw River near the border of North and South Carolina, and the Woccon further north. The explorer John Lawson wrote down a list of Woccon words in 1709, almost all that is known of their language, which is close to Catawba.

They farmed maize, fished and hunted in the swamps and pine forests. Their neighbours included the Winyah, the Pee Dee and the Cape Fear Indians.

English traders from South Carolina bought deerskins and captives from them, and many were caught up in the Yamasee War of 1715. Survivors joined the Catawba or stayed in the swamps. The Waccamaw Siouan Tribe of North Carolina claims descent from them.
